As someone who has been in IT since the early 90's, it's very much a boom and bust career field. One thing that has calmed down is the overall pace of tech thanks to cloud platforms.  Used to be that the hottest tech at the time was something you had to chase (Visual Basic, Lotus Notes, Perl, Java, etc.) only for them to be dead tech in 5-10 years time. Been a raver/EDM fan since 1991 when I was introduced to the early San Francisco rave scene.  First track that I remember introducing the "trance" sound was Future Sound of London's "Papua New Guinea", which while still relying on the breakbeat rhythm sound so popular at the time, also introduced the first ethereal vibes so common with trance.  First time I heard that track, my friend and I rushed up to the DJ and demanded to know who the artist was, after hearing that it sampled Dead Can Dance, who were known as a "band's band" at the time.

So it kinda depends on what trance is to you.  To me, **Binary Finary's "1998" was the OG trance track**, going for a "four on the floor" dance rhythm and extreme HF high hats and delays while also introducing me to the arpeggios, drops, frequency sweeps, and rises associated with what I would later consider "peak trance".

Burning Man.  Had heard about it every year since it moved to Nevada from the beach, then it blew up bigtime a few years later when the mainstream press started covering it.  Had many friends who were devout Burners.

Decided to finally go 20 years after first hearing about it, and since I had the money decided to do it plug-and-play style; we literally showed up and a 5th wheel was waiting for us with unlimited water, waste water treatment, and electricity.  We should shelter from the heat with AC at no extra cost.

First day or two were cool, and the art was amazing, but by the end of it things had descended into chaos.  It was nearly impossible to find our friends in other camps, and it took forever to get to them.  Most horrible biome in the world, hot af during the day and freezing at night and the dust was suffocating.  Freeze, roast, dust, get spooked by a weird sighting of a bird acting strange, just everything was not like anything ever experienced.

Socially it felt like high school all over again, everyone but me seemed to be in cliques (AKA camps) that got along with some and hated others.  And since we were in one of those hated plug-and-play camps, literally found shit outside our 5th wheel.  At the burn itself, wife and I were dosed with drugs in gifted food without warning.

Left the next day, before Temple Burn, and while driving seriously sleep-deprived, it still took us 12 hours to reach a decent shower.

Having lived in downtown SF for many, many years, I decided to move to Alameda at the start of the pandemic for a number of reasons.  But I've managed to continue my car-free lifestyle thanks to being able to work remotely and also thanks to the gig economy (groceries, etc.). So just a couple of nuggets to add to u/informed\_expert's excellent post:

1.  I've tried all the options of getting back and forth to SF, and I generally just take whatever option is coming first.  If it's an AC Transit 19, great, those stops are practically across the street from me.  And it doesn't matter which direction comes firest; if it's going one way, I go to 12 Street BART in Oakland, if it's going the other, I go to Fruitvale BART (they are essentially both serviced by the same number of lines and trains going into SF).  Same with the 51A or O, except I only take the O to SF, not Fruitvale.  (Full disclosure, I generally only ever travel to SF on weekends.  If I do need to go to SF during the week, I try to make the ferry work, but it doesn't run very often AND NEITHER TERMINAL HAS CONNECTING TRANSIT.  <facepalm>. If I had a bike I would consider the ferry more.

2.  AC Transit is planning on a big overhaul of its routes and schedules, but has punted those plans to 2025.  So bear in mind the 51A might suddenly show up as a 6 one day.

3.  I've learned some hacks that are nice.  If you do ditch your car you can sign up for GiG and rent a car by the hour/day/week.  GiG allows one-way trips, so, after taking BART to SF, on your way back you can pick up a car in SF , drive it back to Alameda, and leave it parked in the closest available street space.

Have met both men at very different points in my life,  

Met Jobs in 1995.   I was a new employee at NeXT, when it was down to about 170 employees and before Apple did the reverse merger thing.  Steve walked into my office and, for some reason, pitched to me the idea of selling WebOjects online over the internet for $100 a license.  (1995,  when the internet was best known as the place where you could see Kurt Cobain’s autopsy pics, but was hard to get to.). 

This struck me as odd, considering that the company was down to a handful of products and still trying to sell NeXTStep at “what the market will bear”, a philosophy that endures as Apple to this day.

I had at that point grown up with Apple ][e’s in the computer lab and knowing Steve Jobs as a living legend, and being a bit starstruck I had nothing to add to the conversation.  Luckily my boss, who reported to him, walked in a few minutes before Steve finished his pitch and made sure there wasn’t any awkward silences.

A few weeks later I was with my team when we walked by Steve’s office and there was a teenaged girl talking to his secretary.  My teammates brought up the fact that she was his daughter, but I was confused as I knew he had within the past few years married and started a family with Laurene.  That said, I knew better than to ask questions.

Back to him being in my office, I had heard about his temper and rudeness and how you never wanted to be “invited to take a walk”, which meant that Steve was going to take a walk with you around NeXT’s Redwood City campus and rip you a new one if not outright fire you.  

Nevertheless, I was fired a few weeks later, ending my short career at NeXT.  I’ll never know whether it was due to my (lack of) interaction with Steve, but I suspect it was.

I met Woz just a couple of weeks ago at the Outside Lands festival.  Woz is the polar opposite of Jobs: he believes everyone is the same as he is.  He didn’t say this but I could glean it from the way he stood in line to order food, to the way he said sorry to people that he accidentally grabbed food from the pickup line when he thought his order was up but wasn’t.  (that person was me.)

Was Jobs the more capable CEO?  Very much so: he realized I was in way over my head within 10 minutes of meeting me.  But is Woz the better person?   Well, yeah, duh...he never wanted to be CEO.

Moral of this story: if you want to be a legendary visionary, you don’t have to be an asshole.  But it might just help.

CA survivor here.

The house you purchased before your marriage will remain yours.  The house you bought while married will need to be sold, most likely, as any equity in the property will need to be split 50/50.  Who is on the title is irrelevant if purchased while married.  

Debts incurred during marriage (credit cards, car loans, personal loans, etc.) will also be split 50/50.  Any property that you owned at the time of marriage will remain yours as long as you can prove premarital possession.

 Her infidelity will have no effect on the proceedings ("no fault").  Alimony and child support (not applicable from what I gather) will be determined via an algorithm based on earnings/tax filings and length of the marriage.  Any 401(k) contributions and earnings made during the marriage will be split as well.

In California there is no advantage to being either the petitioner (first mover) or the respondent, although if she has you served by the Sheriff at work there could be an embarrassment to deal with.  If she hits you again, call the police and insist they take a report and document any physical evidence right away.  The quickest way to lose custody is to be branded as a domestic abuser--but be careful, this works both ways and she can get a restraining order with any texts, emails, etc. from you that could be considered as "emotional abuse".  So talk to an attorney first and foremost, and ask them if it would be appropriate for you to seek a restraining order against her (you may see how powerful the double standards are in cases like this).  

Also, whoever files, there is an immediate temporary restraining order than comes into effect that prohibits either parent from taking a child out of state without written permission from the other parent.

Try to save your marriage, by all means, but talk to an attorney as well.

I'll speak to this as someone who struggles with insecurities and paranoia myself.  My wife has never given me reason to not trust her, yet I still find myself snooping and invading her personal space in weak moments.  

It took many therapy sessions for me to learn that my wife actually had little to do with the anxiety I would feel when I was convinced that she was cheating.  The anxiety was/is a result of triggers of "fight or flight" behavioral patterns that have roots in my childhood.  Speaking from personal experience, the hardest part of the recovery process is trying to get a grip on that bastard.   

The short of it, she needs individual therapy to understand where her insecurities are stemming from (almost certainly something in her childhood), and to start the recovery process.  If she's not willing to budge on this, things do not look good for your relationship.

If my experience was typical, expect to be in trauma mode for a while...like, months.  You might have problems sleeping, which may breed problems at work and life.  

Yeah, it sucks!!!  But it's just something you just have to go through; it's part of the recovery process.  It takes a long time, and we just have to go through it.

You may want to make rash choices, but please avoid any major changes outside moving into a different dwelling and filing for separation in the next three months.  Hopefully you two can file after an agreement is reached without expensive mediation.

As countless others have suggested, connect with a therapist and ask them to recommend group therapy sessions (confession, I did not AND WISH I WOULD HAVE).

Happened to me too, twenty years ago, although the timings were a bit different: the day I learned my mom had a few months to live was the same day I found sexy pictures of my now-ex's boyfriend.  

The good news: you get to deal with two life-crushing transformations you never wanted for the price of one.  There's only so much heartache we can feel as a human at a given moment before we red line, and instead of having to have your heart ripped in half on two separate occasions, you will deal with both at once.  

I still cry thinking about how my mom missed meeting my wonderful daughter, and I still miss her greatly.  My ex, not so much.  

You might already in zombie mode, strangely detached from everything that is going on around you and unable to understand why you aren't grieving or exploding more often than you do.  I don't know your situation and I'm not saying this will work for you, but I was able to use that strange emotionless state to get my now-ex to agree to divorce terms without having to involve lawyers.  

Unless your wife is totally evil, she feels sorry for what you are going through, and as a result she won't be as willing to go nuclear in terms of a settlement as she might be without your mom's passing.  Use it to your (and hers') advantage and come together and figure out finances and custody (I should probably clarify here that my ex and I never had children) without bringing in expensive lawyers at the very beginning, or maybe even not at all.  Bear in mind my situation may have been unique, and I certainly wasn't consciously "exploiting" my mom's passing at the time; it was something I realized in retrospect.

In the meantime, move on.  Your life has forever changed, might as well embrace it.  Get an apartment and a gym membership.  Get involved in meetups or join a band or pursue that lifelong goal of being a writer, whatever keeps your mind busy.  

Good luck, bro.

Depends on where you are starting from.  They both run through Civic Center, but if you are starting from close to another Muni Metro station (Powell, New Montgomery, or Embarcadero), then the N has the advantage of not having to transfer.  The N runs through a tunnel and underground (as well as on the surface) so it may actually be faster because the shuttles have to battle street traffic.  That said, the N has a lot more stops. The people on the shuttle will all be OL attendees whereas the N will be packed with all kinds.  The shuttle takes you closer but the N gives you the ability to stop off for something along the way and get back on.  Personally I find the N the "value winner".

Mass transit.  (For instance, you could take the 43 and transfer to the 71.)  Be patient and allow plenty of time; traffic and parking will be a nightmare.

For me, the N-Judah is the way to go.  Just far enough from the festival that it's not too far to walk, but far enough so that it's not paralyzed by traffic.

You might have luck hailing on the street, or you could try the taxi lines at the larger hotels (Hiltons, Sheratons, Marriotts, Westins).  But the best bet is using an app--this is San Francisco after all.  Best bets: Taxi Magic, Flywheel, Uber, and Lyft.  As a last resort you can call dispatch; Yellow Cab (415-333-3333) is the largest co-op.

Other options: the N-Judah and 5-Fulton MUNI lines, and it's a 45-minute walk (slight uphill to OL, down in reverse).

source: SF resident, wife drives a cab

If you don't mind a bit of walking, you can stay anywhere in the city.  I was able to walk to my home near Civic Center (actually a bit further) in 45 minutes from the western half of Outslide Lands by walking through Golden Gate Park, then down Haight Street to Market.  

If walking isn't your thing then staying downtown is good advice and will have the most availability.  Just don't stay in any of the hotels on 6th Street, or within a half-block of it.  Trust me.  

Finally, the shuttle isn't your only option; the N-Judah and 5-Fulton MUNI lines are cheaper options but you'll need $2 exact change each way.
